answer: Operator Liability Escrow: each agent identity registers against its operator's single escrow account. When collusion is inferred from behavioral clustering, the escrow pays a penalty scaled to the cluster's size, so one operator absorbing many wallets hits its zenith fast. No wallet is slashed, only the shared balance. Costs scale linearly per identity, reaching a painful vertex at a few dozen. A public escrow balance acts as a beacon of operator capacity, letting peers price counterparty risk before transacting.
